categoryNote: Power Management entries NX09-001..NX09-015. Boundary rules (TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md): processor min/max/boost/EPP/parking (the whole SUB_PROCESSOR subgroup 54533251-82be-4824-96c1-47b60b740d00) are NX03 territory - NX09 never configures them and New-NxCustomPowerPlan hard-rejects such overrides. Laptops keep independent AC/DC values everywhere: every per-plan capture queries and journals the AC and DC index SEPARATELY. Plan lifecycle policy (adopt register #14, docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md; XOS r1; Vain's delete-all is the rejected inverse): never delete the active plan - switch away first; delete only journal-recorded NEXTRIX-created plans; stock schemes (Balanced 381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e, High performance 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c, Power saver a1841308-3541-4fab-bc81-f71556f20b4a live-verified, Ultimate Performance template e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61) are never mutated or deleted. powercfg /restoredefaultschemes is forbidden in NEXTRIX (destroys every custom plan on the machine). The powercfg /query parser targets the documented English output format and fails closed on localized systems (no verified capture = no mutation); NX09-009's registry route is locale-independent. This file is the single source of truth for NX09; the playbook build is generated from it.

tweaks.name: Active power plan selection
tweaks.description: Switches the active power scheme to a user-chosen, existing plan with the exact previous selection journaled.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner pin a documented, existing power scheme without losing the exact prior selection.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxActivePowerPlan (src/nxcore/functions/NX09.ps1) resolves the target - stock aliases Balanced/HighPerformance/PowerSaver, the NEXTRIX-provisioned Ultimate Performance plan (NX09-002), or an explicit GUID - and refuses to activate any scheme not present in powercfg /list (hidden-by-default schemes are reported honestly, never auto-provisioned inside selection; provisioning is NX09-002/003 territory). Journal-first: the current active scheme GUID and name are captured via powercfg /getactivescheme and journaled BEFORE powercfg /setactive runs; verification re-reads the active scheme and compares GUIDs. Idempotent: an already-active target journals a skip (AlreadyAtState) and mutates nothing. Rollback (Invoke-Nx09Rollback) switches back to the journaled GUID only-if-ours - a manually changed active scheme is reported diverged, never clobbered; a deleted original plan is reported and nothing is guessed. Laptop guidance: plan choice is plane-agnostic (each plan carries independent AC and DC values inside it), so P3 owners wanting aggressive AC behavior should pair this with NX09-003 custom plans whose DC values preserve battery behavior rather than activating stock High/Ultimate plans whose DC values are equally aggressive.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: Balanced (381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e) is active on clean installs; other stock schemes may be hidden until duplicated.
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen, existing scheme is active; the previous scheme GUID is journaled for exact restore.

verify.procedure: Get-NxActivePowerScheme re-read returns the selected GUID; the journal verify entry records Verified (pipeline step 10).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-001 restores the journaled prior active scheme via powercfg /setactive only-if-ours; a deleted prior scheme or a manually changed active scheme is reported diverged, never guessed.

originalState.method: Active scheme GUID + friendly name captured from powercfg /getactivescheme (parsed, fail-closed) and journaled before any switch.

sideEffects: The switch is immediate and applies to both AC and DC planes of the newly active plan (planes stay independent inside the plan).
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (ApplyPowerPlan.bat: switch-away-first lifecycle, per-value results log)

tweaks.name: Ultimate Performance provisioning
tweaks.description: Provisions the documented Ultimate Performance scheme as a NEXTRIX-owned duplicate under a fixed NEXTRIX GUID, without activating it.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner access to the Ultimate Performance scheme while keeping every stock scheme restorable and the created plan exactly deletable.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Add-NxUltimatePerformancePlan duplicates the documented hidden template scheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61 (WinUtil r5 duplicates the same GUID; XOS r1 uses template-derived creation) into the fixed NEXTRIX GUID 6e657472-6978-4e58-5452-4958504c414e via powercfg /duplicatescheme, then names it 'NEXTRIX Ultimate Performance' via /changename. Provisioning ALONE never activates the plan (activation is NX09-001) and never touches stock schemes. The journal records the CREATED GUID (destination form first; on older builds that reject an explicit destination GUID the generated GUID is parsed from the duplicatescheme output and journaled instead) plus the prior-active scheme - so rollback deletes ONLY our plan, refuses stock GUIDs by hard guard, and NEVER deletes while our plan is active (switch away to the journaled prior-active scheme first, documented stock fallback Balanced if that plan is gone, divergence noted). Idempotent: an existing NEXTRIX-named plan at the destination GUID journals AlreadyProvisioned; a non-NEXTRIX plan occupying the GUID is refused untouched. Laptop trade-off honesty: WinUtil ships this family labeled 'Performance Plans - NOT FOR LAPTOPS' (r5); the Ultimate template's DC values are as aggressive as its AC values, so P3 is excluded from this entry's profiles and the battery guidance lives in NX09-001/NX09-003.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: the Ultimate Performance template scheme is hidden; clean installs list only Balanced (and whatever the OEM/user created).
tweaks.proposedState: A NEXTRIX-owned 'Ultimate Performance' duplicate exists under the NEXTRIX GUID, journaled for exact deletion; stock schemes untouched; active plan unchanged.

verify.procedure: powercfg /list parse shows the NEXTRIX GUID with the NEXTRIX plan name; the journal verify entry records Verified; all stock schemes still listed.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-002 deletes only the journal-recorded created GUID - never while it is active (switches away to the journaled prior-active scheme first, Balanced fallback with divergence note), never stock schemes (hard guard); stock schemes remain restorable by construction because they were never touched.

originalState.method: Prior active scheme GUID + the created plan GUID + the template GUID journaled before creation (journal-first); destination occupancy checked against powercfg /list before any mutation.

sideEffects: One additional power scheme appears in the picker; provisioning alone changes no active behavior (plan activation is NX09-001).
documentationSource: research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (Invoke-WPFUltimatePerformance duplicates e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61; category labeled NOT FOR LAPTOPS)
research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (template-derived creation into a fixed GUID; delete never while active)

tweaks.name: Custom NEXTRIX plan generation
tweaks.description: Generates a custom NEXTRIX power plan from a template duplicate and applies user-authored per-plan overrides with full journal linkage.
tweaks.objective: One journaled lifecycle for an owner-authored plan: template-derived creation, per-override capture, verified apply, and reverse-order restoration before deletion.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: New-NxCustomPowerPlan (XOS ApplyPowerPlan pattern, r1): duplicates a chosen template (default: the current active scheme; explicit stock/hidden templates accepted) into the fixed NEXTRIX custom GUID 6e657472-6978-4e58-5452-49584353544d, names it, and then applies the user-authored override list. Every override is validated BEFORE any mutation (atomic refusal - no half-created plans): required subgroup/setting GUIDs, at least one plane set, and a hard NX03 boundary rejection for anything in the processor subgroup (min/max/boost/EPP/parking are NX03 territory). Each override then runs the full pipeline against the NEW plan: both AC and DC indexes captured separately from the fresh template values, journaled, setacvalueindex/setdcvalueindex, re-query verified, journaled. Mechanism ownership: NX09-004..007/010 own the named stock settings on existing plans; NX09-003's overrides are the user's own composition on the plan it created - per the catalogue the plan is importable/exportable via NX09-013. Rollback restores each override in reverse journal order (per-plane only-if-ours) and THEN deletes the plan - never stock, never while active (switch away first to the journaled prior-active scheme, Balanced fallback noted as divergence).
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX custom plan exists; the machine keeps its stock/OEM scheme set.
tweaks.proposedState: A NEXTRIX custom plan exists under the NEXTRIX GUID with every journaled override verified; exportable via NX09-013; active plan unchanged unless NX09-001 selects it.

verify.procedure: powercfg /list shows the created plan with the NEXTRIX name; every journaled override re-queries to its target value with AC and DC verified separately.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-003: every override's journaled original AC and DC values are restored in reverse order (per-plane only-if-ours), then the created plan is deleted - never while active (switch away first), never stock (hard guard).

originalState.method: Prior active scheme + created plan GUID + template GUID journaled at creation; each override's original AC and DC indexes (the fresh plan's template values) captured and journaled before its mutation.

sideEffects: One additional power scheme appears; a failing override aborts cleanly by deleting the just-created plan (nothing left behind).
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (ApplyPowerPlan.bat: template-derived plan, ~45 AC/DC overrides, hidden-setting unhide NOT adopted here - NX09 configures only visible settings; per-value results log)

tweaks.name: PCIe ASPM link policy
tweaks.description: Configures the per-plan PCIe Link State Power Management (ASPM) policy with AC and DC captured, journaled and restorable separately.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner choose an explicit ASPM policy per plane (0=Off, 1=Moderate, 2=Maximum power savings) with exact rollback.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxPcieAspm targets SUB_PCIEXPRESS (501a4d13-42af-4429-9fd1-a8218c268e20) :: ASPM (ee12f906-d277-404b-b6da-e5fa1a576df5), values 0/1/2 as documented. Both planes are captured via the shared powercfg /query parser (AC index and DC index parsed separately, fail-closed on unparseable output - no capture means no mutation), journaled in one original descriptor, then only the requested planes are written via powercfg /setacvalueindex and /setdcvalueindex on the chosen plan (default: active). Verification re-queries and compares BOTH indexes. Trade-off honesty: lower ASPM saves power at the cost of link re-training latency on wake-active devices (documented behavior); NEXTRIX records the configuration intent and claims no latency metric (per TWEAK_CLASSIFICATION.md performance claims remain PENDING until owner evidence at E2+).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: Balanced plans use Moderate/Maximum savings per plane as Windows/OEM policy defines.
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen plan's ASPM AC and DC values equal the user-selected indexes, journaled with both original planes.

verify.procedure: powercfg /query re-read of the setting returns the chosen AC and DC indexes; journal verify entry records Verified with both planes.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-004 restores the journaled original AC and DC indexes per plane, only-if-ours (a plane changed by the user or another tool after apply is reported diverged, never clobbered).

originalState.method: Both the AC and DC index captured separately from powercfg /query BEFORE any change (fail-closed parse) and journaled in the original descriptor.

sideEffects: ASPM changes apply to all PCIe devices honoring the plan policy; a mismatched device/driver may reject the mode (honest limitation - verification is plan-level, not device-level).

tweaks.name: USB selective suspend policy
tweaks.description: Configures the per-plan USB selective suspend policy with AC and DC journaled separately; never touches per-device checkbox values.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner choose the plan-level USB selective suspend state per plane (0=Disabled, 1=Enabled) with exact rollback and honest symptom context.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxUsbSelectiveSuspend targets SUB_USB (2a737441-1930-4402-8d77-b2bebba308a3) :: USB selective suspend (48e6b7a6-50f5-4782-a5d4-53bb8f07e226), values 0/1. Both planes captured via the shared parser and journaled; only requested planes written. Scope honesty: this is the PLAN-level policy only - per-device 'Allow the computer to turn off this device' checkbox values under the Enum tree are deliberately NOT touched (blanket Enum power-value zeroing is on the rejected list); per-device inspection data lives in NX08-007 and feeds the decision. Documented symptom class: selective suspend is the standard first suspect for USB device reconnection drops (keyboards/mice/audio) - that trade-off (power vs peripheral stability) is stated, and the outcome on any specific device remains PENDING until owner evidence (E2+).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: selective suspend enabled on most plans (driver-dependent).
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen plan's USB selective suspend AC and DC values equal the user-selected indexes, journaled with both original planes.

verify.procedure: powercfg /query re-read returns the chosen AC and DC indexes; journal verify entry records Verified with both planes.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-005 restores the journaled original AC and DC indexes per plane, only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Both the AC and DC index captured separately from powercfg /query before any change (fail-closed parse) and journaled.

sideEffects: Disabling suspend keeps USB controllers active (power draw); enabling it may re-suspend idle devices (the documented disconnect symptom class is the honest trade-off).
documentationSource: TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX08-007 (USB controller & HID inspection feeds this decision; XREF)

tweaks.name: Display timeout configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the per-plan display-off timeout in seconds, AC and DC independent by design.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner exact, rollback-safe control of when the display turns off on AC vs battery.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxDisplayTimeout targets SUB_VIDEO (7516b95f-f776-4464-8c53-06167f40cc99) :: VIDEOIDLE (3c0bc021-c8a8-4e07-a973-6b14cbcb2b7e), seconds. The AC and DC indexes are captured separately via the shared powercfg /query parser, journaled in one original descriptor carrying both planes, then only the requested planes are written. Verification re-queries both planes. The two planes are never coupled: changing AC seconds never alters DC seconds and vice versa - this is the AC/DC independence the architecture mandates for every display/sleep/lid entry.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: AC typically 10-15 minutes, DC typically 1-5 minutes on laptops (OEM-dependent).
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen plan's display timeout AC and DC seconds equal the user-selected values, journaled with both original planes.

verify.procedure: powercfg /query re-read returns the chosen AC and DC second values; journal verify entry records Verified with both planes.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-006 restores the journaled original AC and DC seconds per plane, only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Both the AC and DC index captured separately from powercfg /query before any change (fail-closed parse) and journaled.

sideEffects: A zero display timeout (never off) increases idle power draw, especially on battery - stated plainly as a user preference, not an optimization.

tweaks.name: Sleep configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the per-plan sleep (standby) timeout in seconds with AC/DC independence, and includes a read-only wake-source inspection.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner exact, rollback-safe control of standby timing per plane, with visibility into what can wake the machine.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxSleepTimeout targets SUB_SLEEP (238c9fa8-0aad-41ed-83f4-97be242c8f20) :: STANDBYIDLE (29f6c1db-86da-48c5-9fdb-f2b67b1f44da), seconds. Both planes captured separately, journaled, requested planes written via setacvalueindex/setdcvalueindex, re-query verified. The result object carries a read-only wake-source report: powercfg /lastwake raw text plus the /devicequery wake_armed device list - inspection only, NEXTRIX never disables wake devices here. Capability honesty: the sleep timeout applies to whatever standby model the firmware exposes (powercfg /a context is informational; S0 Low Power Idle systems idle differently from S3 systems); hibernate-after timing is NX09-008 territory.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: AC sleep often disabled on desktops, enabled after 10-30 minutes on laptops; DC shorter.
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen plan's standby timeout AC and DC seconds equal the user-selected values, journaled with both original planes, plus a wake-source report.

verify.procedure: powercfg /query re-read returns the chosen AC and DC second values; journal verify entry records Verified with both planes; wake-source report populated read-only.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-007 restores the journaled original AC and DC seconds per plane, only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Both the AC and DC index captured separately from powercfg /query before any change (fail-closed parse) and journaled.

sideEffects: Zero standby timeout keeps the machine from sleeping on that plane (power draw trade-off, user preference); wake-armed devices are reported but never modified.

tweaks.name: Hibernate configuration
tweaks.description: Enables or disables hibernation via the documented powercfg /h, with the original state journaled from the registry anchor.
tweaks.objective: Exact on/off control of hibernation with honest disk-space and dual-boot trade-offs.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxHibernate journals the original state first: the HibernateEnabled registry descriptor (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power, captured via Capture-NxRegistryValue with existence/kind/value), the co-managed HiberFileSizePercent context, and the powercfg /a S4 availability (informational - the registry value is the authoritative anchor). Only then does it run powercfg /h on|off (the documented command, which also manages hiberfil.sys). Verification re-captures the registry anchor and compares; on failure the original direction is restored best-effort. Trade-offs stated honestly: DISABLING frees disk space roughly the size of RAM (or the configured percentage) and removes the hibernation power state; it also disables Fast Startup at the machine level (NX09-009 interplay - enabling Fast Startup requires hibernation on). DUAL-BOOT: hibernation (and Fast Startup's hybrid shutdown) can leave NTFS volumes mounted-dirty from the other OS's perspective, causing checkdisk/lock behaviors - dual-boot owners are cautioned in the recommendation text. Restore via /h back to the journaled direction is verified against the anchor; custom hiberfile sizing is out of scope (HiberFileSizePercent is journaled as context only).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: hibernation enabled on most laptops (S4-capable), often already disabled on OEM desktop images.
tweaks.proposedState: HibernateEnabled equals the chosen direction; journaled with the exact original descriptor.

verify.procedure: HibernateEnabled re-capture equals the chosen value; journal verify entry records Verified; /a S4 availability recorded as context (firmware without S4 support is reported honestly, never fabricated).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-008 runs powercfg /h back to the journaled original direction only-if-ours (current HibernateEnabled must still equal the recorded modified value); verification re-captures the anchor.

originalState.method: HibernateEnabled exact registry descriptor (path/kind/existed/value) + HiberFileSizePercent context + /a S4 availability captured and journaled before any change.

sideEffects: Toggling /h creates or deletes hiberfil.sys (disk space in the size class of RAM or the configured percent); dual-boot NTFS dirty-mount interplay documented above.
documentationSource: research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (WPFTweaksHiber pairs /hibernate off with HibernateEnabled - NEXTRIX uses /h only, registry as anchor)

tweaks.name: Fast Startup configuration
tweaks.description: Enables or disables Fast Startup via the documented HiberbootEnabled registry value, journaled exactly.
tweaks.objective: Exact, locale-independent control of Fast Startup with the original value restorable to the byte (kind and existence included).
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxFastStartup runs the standard registry pipeline on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power :: HiberbootEnabled (documented as the Fast Startup toggle): exact original captured via Capture-NxRegistryValue (key existence, value existence, kind, data - the value can be ABSENT on fresh installs and that fact is journaled), journal-first apply via Set-NxRegistryValue (DWord 1=enabled/0=disabled), then Test-NxConfigurationState read-back verification. Capability honesty: Fast Startup functions only while hibernation is enabled - when /h off is active the configuration still holds but has no effect, and the function reports that note explicitly (the hibernate decision belongs to NX09-008, never auto-coupled here; contrast WinUtil r5 which couples /hibernate off with HibernateEnabled=0 - rejected as coupling). DUAL-BOOT TRADE-OFFS (mandatory context, documented by Microsoft and in the reference ecosystem): Fast Startup performs a hybrid shutdown whose saved kernel session can (a) leave NTFS volumes flagged dirty for other operating systems, forcing their checkdisk or mounting them read-only, (b) prevent BitLocker auto-unlock from completing as on a cold boot, and (c) wake-on-LAN behaves differently after hybrid shutdown. Dual-boot and drive-encryption owners should keep it disabled - the recommendation text states this.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: HiberbootEnabled present and 1 (Fast Startup on) on most installs; absent on some images.
tweaks.proposedState: HiberbootEnabled equals the chosen DWord value with the exact original journaled (existence + kind + data).

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState read-back of HiberbootEnabled equals the chosen DWord; journal verify entry records Verified; capability note reports when hibernation is currently unavailable (config-held vs effective-function distinction).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-009 restores the exact original: value rewritten with its original kind; a value that never existed is deleted (only-if-ours first - divergence reported, never clobbered).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue records key existence, value existence, kind and exact data for HiberbootEnabled before any change.

sideEffects: Fast Startup changes next-boot behavior only (no restart required to configure); the dual-boot/BitLocker/WoL trade-offs are documented above and restated in the recommendation text.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/power/distinguishing-fast-startup-from-wake-from-hibernate (HiberbootEnabled documented as the Fast Startup toggle)

tweaks.name: Lid close behavior (laptops)
tweaks.description: Configures the lid-close action per plan with AC and DC independent, laptop-gated.
tweaks.objective: Let laptop owners choose 'do nothing while docked / sleep on battery' style behavior with exact rollback.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxLidCloseAction targets SUB_BUTTONS (4f971e89-eebd-4455-a8de-9e59040e7347) :: Lid close action (5ca83367-6e45-459f-a27b-476b1d01c936 - GUID verified against the live PowerSettings store on 2026-11-23; the commonly mis-cited 5ca8fa67 variant does not exist there), values 0=Do nothing, 1=Sleep, 2=Hibernate, 3=Shut down. Both planes are captured separately via the shared powercfg /query parser and journaled; only the requested planes are written. Plans that lack the lid setting (desktop plans) are skipped gracefully with that exact reason - the parser reports setting-not-found and the function refuses to invent anything. requiredHardware gates this entry to Laptop chassis (battery-first classifier per NxHardware).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: lid close sleeps on both planes on most laptops.
tweaks.proposedState: The chosen plan's lid action AC and DC values equal the user-selected indexes, journaled with both original planes.

verify.procedure: powercfg /query re-read returns the chosen AC and DC lid action indexes; journal verify entry records Verified with both planes; on lid-less plans the skip reason names setting-not-found honestly.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-010 restores the journaled original AC and DC indexes per plane, only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Both the AC and DC index captured separately from powercfg /query before any change (fail-closed parse) and journaled.

sideEffects: 'Do nothing' on AC keeps the machine running hot in a closed lid while docked - stated as a user preference with a thermal note (NX10 monitoring is read-only).

tweaks.name: OEM battery conservation reporting
tweaks.description: Read-only reporting of OEM battery conservation interfaces - existence-level detection, uncertainty-marked, no writes ever.
tweaks.objective: Surface which OEM battery utility interfaces exist on the machine without touching firmware or OEM services.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxOemBatteryConservationState probes interface PRESENCE only: the Lenovo ImController power-plugin key and root\Lenovo WMI namespace, plus ASUS/Dell/HP utility registry trees. Wherever no vendor-documented read contract exists - which is the current state for every OEM's conservation/charge-threshold mode - the state is reported 'Unknown' with an explicit uncertainty note; NEXTRIX never fabricates a readable state and never writes firmware (directive; NX10's no-firmware-writes rule applies to this whole family). The report is the deliverable: owners manage the actual mode in their OEM utility. E0 because the interfaces are community-known but the states are not vendor-documented.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX report; OEM conservation state managed invisibly by the OEM utility.
tweaks.proposedState: A report listing detected OEM interfaces with per-probe Unknown/uncertainty marks and noWritesPerformed=true.

verify.procedure: Report enumerates every probe with interfaceDetected, state (Unknown unless documented), uncertainty note and provenance; noWritesPerformed=true.

documentationSource: research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (OEM power-settings family referenced; no conservation-mode state contract anywhere)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX09 row (detection only where OEM exposes an interface)

tweaks.name: OEM performance mode detection
tweaks.description: Read-only detection of OEM performance-mode utility layers - service presence reported, mode state marked Unknown, no firmware writes.
tweaks.objective: Tell the owner which OEM utility layer is present so mode switching stays an explicit OEM-tool decision.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxOemPerformanceMode enumerates services whose display names match known OEM utility families (Armoury Crate/MyASUS, Lenovo Vantage, Dell SupportAssist, HP power/thermal utilities, Omen/Legion/Gigabyte/MSI center families) and reports each match with status. The actual performance-mode STATE is reported 'Unknown' with an explicit uncertainty note: current OEM stacks expose no documented, scriptable state contract. NEXTRIX never writes firmware and never switches modes (catalogue directive; mode switching, where an interface is documented, belongs to NX10-006 per-OEM modules). Detection feeds recommendation text only - no configuration follows from it automatically.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX report; OEM performance mode managed invisibly by the OEM utility.
tweaks.proposedState: A report listing detected OEM utility services with status and an Unknown-marked mode state plus provenance; noWritesPerformed=true.

verify.procedure: Report lists matched services with display names and status; modeState=Unknown with uncertainty note; noWritesPerformed=true.

documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (XOS MSPower_DeviceEnable WMI sweep is the REJECTED inverse - NEXTRIX reports instead of writing)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX10-006 (per-OEM module ownership for any documented switching)

tweaks.name: Power plan export/import/restore tooling
tweaks.description: Journaled .pow export of any existing plan to a user-chosen path, and journal-linked import under an explicit GUID with guarded restore.
tweaks.objective: File-level plan portability that supports NX16 rollback bundles and never destroys stock or active plans.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Export-NxPowerPlan runs powercfg /export to a user-chosen folder (timestamped NEXTRIX-powerplan-<guid>.pow) or explicit file path; an existing file requires -Force (never silently overwritten); export is additive (configuration untouched, stock schemes exportable - they are only read). Import-NxPowerPlan runs powercfg /import from a user-chosen .pow into an explicit target GUID with three hard guards: stock GUIDs refused outright, the ACTIVE plan refused outright, and any existing plan at the GUID requires -AllowOverwrite consent (journaled). Both operations journal the active scheme, the involved GUID and the file path before/with the operation, and both verify (file exists non-empty / imported GUID appears in /list). Restore path (Invoke-Nx09Rollback): an imported plan is deleted under the same lifecycle guards as NX09-002/003 - never the active plan (switch away first), never stock, only the journal-recorded GUID; exports are additive and intentionally not rolled back. powercfg /restoredefaultschemes is forbidden (it would destroy every custom plan on the machine - the exact anti-pattern adopt register #14 rejects).
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX .pow exports or imports; plans live and die on the machine only.
tweaks.proposedState: A .pow backup at the user-chosen path (journaled), and/or an imported plan under the explicit GUID (journaled, deletable via rollback).

verify.procedure: Export: the .pow file exists at the chosen path with non-zero size and is journaled; Import: powercfg /list shows the imported GUID and the journal records it.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx09Rollback -TweakId NX09-013 deletes ONLY the journal-recorded imported plan (never stock, never the active plan - switch away first); exports are additive and remain on disk untouched.

originalState.method: Active scheme, exported/imported GUID and file paths journaled with each operation; import additionally records prior-active scheme and any -AllowOverwrite consent.

sideEffects: Files land only at user-chosen paths; import adds one plan to the picker.

tweaks.name: Energy report (powercfg /energy)
tweaks.description: Runs the documented powercfg /energy analysis and writes the report to a user-chosen folder; no configuration is changed.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner Microsoft's own energy-efficiency findings (error/warning/info classes) as evidence for power decisions.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxEnergyReport runs powercfg /energy /duration <seconds> /output <chosen folder>\NEXTRIX-energy-report-<timestamp>.htm. The system is observed for the chosen duration (default 60 s) before the report is generated - a side effect of time, not of configuration. The report file is the only output; nothing in the power configuration is touched. When a journal is initialized the report run is journaled as an additive powerDiagnostic record (changedConfiguration=false). Elevated privileges are required by the command itself (documented); the output path is always user-chosen - NEXTRIX never writes reports to implicit system locations.
tweaks.proposedState: An energy-report.htm at the user-chosen folder, journaled as a read-only diagnostic.

verify.procedure: The .htm report exists at the chosen folder with non-zero size; exit code and truncated output sample returned with the result.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic (the report file stays until the owner deletes it).

sideEffects: Takes at least the configured duration to observe; brief tracing activity during that window.

tweaks.name: Battery report (powercfg /batteryreport)
tweaks.description: Runs the documented battery usage report to a user-chosen folder; read-only, battery-gated.
tweaks.objective: Give laptop owners Microsoft's own battery health/usage history as decision evidence.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxBatteryReport runs powercfg /batteryreport /output <chosen folder>\NEXTRIX-battery-report-<timestamp>.html. Read-only; the HTML report (capacity history, recent usage, battery drains) is the only output, journaled as an additive powerDiagnostic record when a journal is present. Battery-gated via requiredHardware.chassis=Laptop; on battery-less desktops the entry is ineligible and the underlying command failure would be reported honestly (exit code + sample, nothing fabricated). Classifier caveat recorded honestly: NxHardware's battery-first classifier can mistake a USB UPS for a laptop battery (Win32_Battery enumerates some UPS devices) - such a machine would produce a degenerate report, not a wrong configuration.
tweaks.proposedState: A battery-report.html at the user-chosen folder, journaled as a read-only diagnostic.

verify.procedure: The .html report exists at the chosen folder with non-zero size; exit code and output sample returned with the result.

sideEffects: Writes one report file to the user-chosen folder.
